newsitem.title: CHINA: China orders abolition of futures settlement limit.
newsitem.headline: China orders abolition of futures settlement limit.

text.p: China's top securities watchdog has ordered commodity futures exchanges to abolish a settlement system that sets limits on the total amount for physical delivery, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) in a recent circular ordered all exchanges to stop using settlement limits for empty and new contracts with immediate effect, the newspaper said.
It gave no explanation for the move and did not say when the new regulations had taken effect.

Shanghai traders said settlement limits in many of China's 15 futures exchanges made it possible for wealthy institutions to build up huge long positions waiting for a short-squeeze when a delivery date was approaching. This had to some extent encouraged institutional market manipulation, they said.

The move is the latest step in a sweeping crackdown on China's fledgling futures markets in the past few months, analysts said. Angered by repeated violations of rules and rampant irregularities, Beijing has stressed restrictions rather than development as the keynote for the futures markets in the crackdown, they said.
The CSRC circular ordered all exchanges to unify their morning trading hours to 9.00-11.30 a.m. and in the afternoon from 1.30 to 3.00 p.m. starting from January 1, 1997, the newspaper said.
It also ordered all exchanges to strengthen management of appointed physical delivery warehouses.
The exchanges "must revoke the licence for those delivery warehouses that provide convenience for market manipulation".
From November 25, the exchanges must make public the 20 members who are most active during the day's trading and their trading volumes after trading ends, the circular said.
The exchanges are also required to make public 20 members who hold the largest long or short positions and the holdings each has after the day's trading, it said.

After trading closes each Friday, the exchanges are required to announce registered warehouse stocks for every contract and the amount of each contract for which members have applied for physical delivery, the circular said.

Within five days of the delivery date, the exchanges must make pubic details of the delivery, including total amount of delivery, who delivered the physical goods and who will receive the goods, the circular said.
